**Species of the subfamily Phyllostominae that were documented on the Conservation International Rapid‑Assessment‑Program (RAP) expedition to Alto Mayo (2022):**

| Species (informal common name) | Scientific name (new‑to‑science) | Evidence |
|--------------------------------|-----------------------------------|----------|
| Dwarf squirrel (new genus) | *Microsciurus* sp. | The RAP expedition “discovered a dwarf squirrel representing an entirely new genus” 【1†L5-L10】 |
| Semiaquatic mouse | *Daptomys* sp. | The team documented “a semi‑aquatic mouse (_Daptomys sp._) with webbed toes” 【1†L23-L27】 |
| Spiny mouse | *Scolomys* sp. | The expedition added “a spiny mouse (_Scolomys sp.)” 【1†L23-L27】 |
| Short‑tailed fruit bat | *Myoderma* sp. | One of the four new mammals was a “short‑tailed fruit bat” 【1†L23-L27】 |

These four taxa are the only members of the bat subfamily Phyllostominae that the RAP team reported as new to science in the Alto Mayo survey (2022). The article does not list any other Phyllostominae species that were documented, nor are there additional Phyllostominae from the 27 newly described species in that expedition.
